claims.text: Thermal expansion mismatch during composite solidification is a primary cause of the unresolved stress–strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal expansion mismatch during composite solidification is a primary cause of the unresolved thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal expansion mismatch generates thermal stresses during composite solidification.
The initial material may contain varying degrees of cold work and aging.
In-situ neutron diffraction under high-temperature deformation can be used to investigate the proposed behavior.
The proposed testing includes tensile, compressive, and thermal loading.
Thermal stresses alter the alloy's microstructure.
Thermal stresses alter the alloy's mechanical properties.
Thermal expansion mismatch and thermal stresses produce changes in strength.
Thermal expansion mismatch and thermal stresses produce changes in ductility.
Room-temperature behavior without thermal loading is the baseline.
The relevant temperature boundary is 293–1250 K.
The hypothesis would be falsified if stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior were not significantly affected by thermal expansion mismatch and thermal stresses.

contradictions.description: The conditions state testing up to 1250 °C, whereas the boundary ends at 1250 K, which is about 977 °C. These are materially different upper temperatures.

The initial state permits uncontrolled variation in cold work and aging, while the proposed baseline and experiment do not match or control those variables. This undermines attribution of differences specifically to thermal-expansion mismatch.
